preamble: The voiceless lateral fricative [ɬ] and the labiodental [f] both have weak, diffuse frication, and listeners whose language lacks [ɬ] can perceive it as [f]. Davis & Alfaifi (2019) document this as a regular change in Upper Faifi Arabic (southwestern Saudi Arabia): root-initial reflexes of Classical Arabic ḍād, pronounced [ɮˤ] in neighbouring dialects, were devoiced and depharyngealized to [ɬ] and reinterpreted as [f]. The authors know of no other documented case of ɬ > f.

examples.note: The [ɬ] stage is posited by the authors from root-initial devoicing and depharyngealization; the change applies only root-initially.
Root-initial even in the plural, where the consonant is no longer word-initial; non-root-initial ḍād surfaces as [ðˤ].

sources: Davis, S., & Alfaifi, A. (2019). A different path to [f]: labiodentalization in Faifi Arabic. Papers in Historical Phonology, 4, 45–61. https://doi.org/10.2218/pihph.4.2019.3072
